title: Safety-lane for pinned model revisions: adaptive spillover, phased warmup, and telemetry-driven rollback
creator: Ava Cheng
description: Goal: implement a 'safety-lane' execution and routing policy for version-pinned models that allows controlled spillover to compatible variants and regions while protecting pinned revisions during deprecation windows. We want automated, telemetry-triggered rollbacks and an orchestrated warmup sequence for spill targets so customer applications experience minimal error spikes or large latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming requests to a pinned model can spill to one or more configured fallback variants/regions under operator-defined policies. 2) Spillover must include a phased warmup: initial 1% traffic, then 10%, then target >X% as capacity stabilizes. 3) KV-cache priming and prefix-caching should be performed on warmup traffic to reduce cold-start p50/95. 4) Observable signals (error_rate, p95_latency, token_generation_errors) must be emitted and surfaced in Console with a preconfigured runbook. 5) Automatic rollback triggers when telemetry breaches defined thresholds for >5 minutes. 6) Soft-deprecation flow starts with a configurable grace period (default 14d) and shows a deprecation banner in Console; during this window, the safety-lane enforces stricter warmup and lower spill ratios. 7) Integration tests + canary in staging show <0.2% additional client-visible errors for 30d canary period.
design_notes: Key ideas: (a) Safety-lane is a router-layer construct that sits between incoming request router and model scheduler. It evaluates policies in order: compatibility, region affinity, latency budget, and deprecation status. (b) Warmup is timeboxed per-variant and includes KV cache priming buckets plus synthetic prefix replay (from recent traffic) to reduce the cold-kv hit rate. (c) Rollback is telemetry-driven: we use composite signal (error_rate > 0.5% AND p95_latency increase >20% relative to baseline) sustained for 5m to immediately shift 100% back to pinned variant and pause further warmups. (d) Console exposes live spill percentages, warmup progress, and 'why' reason codes for each routed request. (e) Soft-deprecation mode lowers spill ceiling to 5% until the grace window has elapsed and requires an explicit operator override to exceed it.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cache priming may create hotspotting on small clusters — mitigation: stagger warmup schedules and limit concurrent warmups per region. Risk: misclassification of compatibility (leading to subtle semantic regressions) — mitigation: require evaluation job that runs customer-supplied prompt-set matches before enabling policy; route a small fraction to human-preview variant. Risk: telemetry noise causing flip-flop — mitigation: require sustained windows + hysteresis and backoff counters.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 2w): prototype router hooks, policy DSL, and synthetic prefix replay; run offline sim on fleet traces. Phase 2 (staging canary, 3w): integrate KV-priming and warmup schedule; expose Console telemetry. Phase 3 (limited production rollout, 2w): enable safety-lane for non-critical tenants with observability and runbook. Phase 4 (optimize, 2w): iterate on thresholds, add auto-quarantine for variants showing semantic drift.
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for policy evaluation; integration tests that assert traffic percentages and cache hit improvements; load test with traffic shape generator (burst + steady) to validate warmup; e2e regression test using canonical prompts; manual runbook drill for rollback. Share test results in PR.
metrics_to_track: p95_latency_change, error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate_during_warmup, spill_percentage, number_of_rollbacks, customer_visible_errors, deprecation_banner_ack_count
